title: Enhanced keratometry for IOL power calculation after myopic LASIK: a multi-device comparison
abstract: Background To comparatively evaluate the predictive accuracy of Lenstar 900, IOL Master 700, OptiWave refractive analysis (ORA) and a modified Placido topography method in patients undergoing cataract surgery following myopic laser-assisted in situ keratomileusis (LASIK). Methods A cohort of 62 post-myopic LASIK eyes from 37 patients was enrolled. Six methods were employed to estimate intraocular lens (IOL) power: Lenstar Barrett true K (BTK), Lenstar Shammas, IOL Master BTK, IOL Master BTK with total keratometry (TK), ORA and a modified Placido topography method. Results Mean prediction errors and mean absolute errors were lowest to highest for the modified Placido topography method, IOL Master BTK with TK and IOL Master BTK, respectively. The IOL Master BTK, Lenstar BTK and ORA method did not significantly differ from each other. All methods outperformed Lenstar Shammas. At 2 months postoperatively, the modified Placido topography method had the highest percentages of eyes with manifest absolute prediction errors within 0.50 and 1.00 D (91.9%, 100%), followed by IOL Master BTK with TK (67.7%, 100%), IOL Master BTK (62.9%, 95.2%), ORA (54.8%, 95.2%), Lenstar BTK (53.2%, 95.2%) and Lenstar Shammas (38.7%, 67.7%). Conclusion The BTK formula was highly accurate in predicting IOL power for patients undergoing cataract surgery after myopic LASIK. However, variations in keratometry values can influence outcomes. In this study, the modified Placido topography method was the most accurate, followed by IOL Master BTK with TK, IOL Master BTK, ORA, Lenstar BTK and Lenstar Shammas.

title: Efficacy and safety of 0.01% atropine in Chinese children with nearwork-induced transient myopia: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
abstract: Background Nearwork-induced transient myopia (NITM) is a temporary reduction in distance vision following prolonged nearwork and is associated with an increased risk of myopia progression. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of 0.01% atropine in controlling NITM in Chinese children. Methods This randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial enrolled Chinese children aged 6-15 years with myopia. Participants were randomised 1:1 to receive 0.01% atropine or placebo eye drops once nightly for 12 weeks, followed by a 12-week observation period. The primary endpoint was the change in initial NITM values from baseline to week 12. Results A total of 148 participants were randomised to the 0.01% atropine group (n = 74) or placebo group (n = 74). The mean change in initial NITM from baseline to week 12 was 0.61 ± 0.31 dioptres (D) in the 0.01% atropine group versus 0.18 ± 0.56 D in the placebo group (P Conclusion Atropine (0.01%) significantly reduces initial NITM values in myopic children, demonstrating sustained benefits up to 12 weeks post-treatment and a favourable safety profile.

title: Multidrug antifungal resistance and clinical outcomes in fungal keratitis: a prospective study in a South Indian population
abstract: Abstract Objectives Our primary objective was to identify the rate of antifungal resistance (including multidrug resistance) of fungal isolates cultured from fungal keratitis patients in South India. Our secondary objective was to identify associations between antifungal resistance and patient outcome. Subjects/methods 153 patients attending the cornea clinic at Aravind Eye Hospital, Madurai (May–August 2025) with culture-positive fungal keratitis were enrolled in the study. Cultured isolates were evaluated for natamycin, amphotericin B, voriconazole and econazole minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC; n = 151–153). MIC data were analysed by Kruskal-Wallis test followed by Dunn’s multiple comparisons. Patient disease outcome relative to isolate resistance was analysed by Fisher’s exact test ( n = 91). Results There were high levels of resistance to all four antifungals, which were significantly elevated in Fusarium spp. and Aspergillus spp. isolates compared to other fungal genera ( P < 0.0001). Fusarium spp. isolates ( n = 81) resistant to: natamycin: 38.3%; amphotericin B: 93.8%; voriconazole: 97.5%; and econazole: 76.5%. Aspergillus spp. isolates ( n = 33) resistant to: natamycin: 66.7%; amphotericin B: 87.9%; voriconazole: 6.1%; and econazole: 0%. Overall, fungal resistance to natamycin significantly correlated with an adverse clinical outcome, P = 0.0034, relative risk 1.7 (95% CI: 1.2–2.6). Conclusions The majority of fungal isolates were resistant to multiple antifungals; none of the Fusarium isolates were susceptible to all four drugs, and 28% were resistant to all of them. Resistance to natamycin may worsen clinical outcome, particularly for infections caused by Aspergillus, even when susceptible to azoles. Our data support the need for species-specific MIC thresholds to have increased clinical utility.

title: Type 4 macular neovascularisation arising from a congenital toxoplasmosis scar
Thirty-year silicone implant granuloma
Restorative and regenerative therapies for vision loss
abstract: Reversing blindness and restoring functional vision remains a central challenge in biomedical engineering. Advances in ocular prosthetics have enabled limited recovery of light perception, motion detection, and coarse object recognition through anterior segment devices such as keratoprostheses and through posterior segment interfaces including retinal, suprachoroidal, optic nerve, and cortical implants. Parallel progress in organ-on-a-chip systems and retinal organoids is providing increasingly sophisticated platforms for disease modelling and therapeutic development. Despite these advances, issues of long-term biocompatibility, signal fidelity, and surgical complexity continue to constrain clinical performance. Emerging approaches that combine stem cell-derived tissues, biofabrication, and hybrid bioelectronic constructs offer promising avenues for next-generation vision restoration, although current production remains limited to early-stage or small-scale systems. Effective integration of these technologies also requires structured vision-rehabilitation strategies to harness neuroplasticity and support functional adaptation. This review synthesises recent progress across prosthetic, rehabilitative, and regenerative domains and outlines key opportunities for future translational development.

title: Three-year real-world outcomes of faricimab in pretreated eyes with treatment-resistant neovascular age-related macular degeneration
abstract: Long-term real-world evidence on faricimab in previously treated, treatment-resistant neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) remains limited. Although pivotal trials demonstrated sustained visual outcomes and extended dosing intervals in treatment-naïve eyes, these findings may not be directly applicable to patients with chronic disease, persistent exudative activity, and a high treatment burden despite frequent anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) therapy [ 1 ]. This study reports three-year outcomes following a switch from aflibercept 2 mg (Eylea; Bayer, Germany) to faricimab (Vabysmo; Roche, Switzerland) in treatment-resistant nAMD, extending the previously published 12- and 24-month analyses of this cohort [ 2 , 3 ].

Risk factors, microbiological profiles, and clinical outcomes of paediatric infectious keratitis: The Midlands Infectious Keratitis Study
abstract: Abstract Objectives To characterise the clinical features, microbiological profiles, and outcomes of paediatric infectious keratitis (IK). Methods This retrospective multicentre study included paediatric patients (≤18 years old) who presented with presumed IK and underwent corneal sampling at two UK tertiary ophthalmic centres. Results We included 42 cases in this study; median age was 13.3 years (IQR 10.1–16.1). Contact lens wear (15, 35.7%) and ocular surface disease (15, 35.7%) were the most common risk factors. Twenty-five (59.5%) cases were microbiologically positive (MP), with Pseudomonas aeruginosa (5, 16.1%), Staphylococcus aureus (5, 16.1%), and Serratia marcescens (5, 16.1%) being the most commonly isolated bacteria. Six (24.0%) cases were caused by polymicrobial infection (≥2 bacteria). Median presenting CDVA was 0.30 logMAR [0.20–1.30] and improved to 0.15 [0.00–0.75] at final follow-up ( p < 0.001). Poor visual outcome (final CDVA > 0.6 logMAR) was observed in 11 (26.2%) cases and was associated with worse presenting CDVA ( p = 0.010), prior corneal surgery ( p = 0.003), and MP status ( p = 0.016). Delayed corneal healing (>30 days) occurred in 17 (40.5%) cases. Complications were uncommon, including 3 (7.1%) recurrence, 2 (4.8%) corneal melt, and 1 (2.4%) perforation. Conclusions Paediatric IK represents an important ocular morbidity in the UK. Contact lens wear was the most common risk factor and was strongly associated with P. aeruginosa infection, highlighting the need for improved awareness, education, and prevention. MP cases were associated with worse visual outcomes and features of greater disease severity. These findings support early recognition and appropriate management to optimise visual outcomes in this population.

title: Systematic review of eyecare Patient-Reported Experience Measures (PREMs) following COSMIN guidelines
abstract: Abstract Patient-Reported Experience Measures (PREMs) are essential for assessing healthcare quality from the patient’s perspective. However, their use in eyecare is limited. This systematic review aimed to assess the existing evidence on the measurement properties of PREMs used to capture patient experiences of eyecare services. A comprehensive literature search was conducted across Web of Science Core Collection, Embase, PubMed, and Scopus to identify studies reporting the development and/or psychometric evaluation of PREMs in eyecare. The extracted measurement properties encompassed information on item development, content validity (the extent to which items are relevant, comprehensive, and understandable), structural validity (whether the items form the right scales), internal consistency (how well items measure underlying eyecare experience domains), cross-cultural validity, reliability, hypothesis testing, and responsiveness. Quality assessment, evaluation of measurement properties, evidence synthesis, and grading followed COSMIN methodology for systematic reviews. Thirteen studies were included, three of which evaluated 10 distinct PREMs, across settings, including low vision and primary/secondary eyecare. All ten PREMs met criteria for COSMIN Category B (potentially recommended, further validation needed). However, most lacked sufficient evidence for content validity and lacked supporting evidence for structural validity. None demonstrated adequate reliability, and none reported using Item Response Theory or Rasch Measurement Theory. Consequently, there was insufficient evidence to classify any of the identified PREMs into COSMIN recommendation Category A (recommended for use). Future studies on PREMs in eyecare should aim to strengthen the evidence for content and structural validity and provide robust proof of their reliability.

A scoping review of integrated blink analysis technologies for ocular surface diseases
abstract: Abstract The purpose of this review is to describe integrated technologies for blink analysis and their utility in evaluating ocular surface diseases. A literature search was conducted using PubMed, Embase, and CENTRAL from January 1, 2000, to August 17, 2025. Search terms included “Eye Blink”, “Blink”, “Blinking”, “Device”, “Technology”, “Appliance”, and “Application”. We included studies describing the use of integrated technologies to capture and analyse blink metrics for the evaluation of dry eye disease and other ocular surface conditions. Publications describing technical engineering aspects or technologies without evaluation of ocular surface diseases were excluded. Findings from relevant studies were extracted and compared. Of 3275 identified records, 42 met inclusion criteria. We evaluated the use of 9 technologies. These comprised desk-bound devices(Intelligent Vision Sensor, LipiView™, and IDRA) , wearable devices (Wink Glass, Blink-sensing Glasses), and smartphone or computer applications(HealthyRoad, DryEyeRhythm, Dry eye or not? and EyeScore) . LipiView™ and IDRA were most commonly studied. Blink rate and partial blink rate were the most commonly analysed parameters, and DED was the most commonly evaluated ocular surface condition. Consistent with existing literature, studies demonstrated associations between increased partial blink rates and ocular surface compromise. There was however heterogeneity in methods of blink analysis and insufficient validation of the accuracy and diagnostic ability of measured blink parameters for ocular surface conditions. Integrated blink analysis technologies are promising for the assessment of ocular surface diseases. Further studies are needed to evaluate the validity, reliability, and clinical utility of these technologies.

Cognitive heuristics in the operating room: the role of ‘left-digit bias’ in ophthalmic surgical selection
abstract: Abstract Introduction Left-digit bias is a cognitive heuristic in which the leftmost digit of a number disproportionately influences judgment. This study evaluates the impact of perceived patient age on ophthalmic surgical decision-making. Methods Using a multicentre federated electronic health record network, patients aged 40–85 years with a routine health visit, followed by at least 1 documented ophthalmic examination and a diagnosis code specific to the surgical outcome under study, were followed for 1 year. Patients were grouped into consecutive 2-year age cohorts and matched 1:1 on demographic characteristics, healthcare utilisation, systemic comorbidities, and ocular diagnoses and procedures. Prespecified decade-boundary comparisons were 48/49 versus 50/51, 58/59 versus 60/61, and 68/69 versus 70/71. Odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated for each surgical outcome. Results Among 8,156,608 eligible patients, 218,816 (2.68%) underwent an included ophthalmic procedure, including 201,591 phacoemulsification procedures. The younger cohort had lower odds of phacoemulsification at each decade boundary: 48/49 vs. 50/51 (OR, 0.956; 95% CI, 0.926–0.986), 58/59 vs. 60/61 (OR, 0.935; 95% CI, 0.909–0.961), and 68/69 vs. 70/71 (OR, 0.903; 95% CI, 0.879–0.927; all P < 0.001). No mid-decade phacoemulsification comparisons were significant. The odds of undergoing MIGS were lower at 48/49 vs. 50/51 (OR, 0.876; 95% CI, 0.814–0.940); no decade-boundary differences were observed for GDI or keratoplasty procedures. Conclusions Consistent with left-digit bias, surgical frequency for phacoemulsification increased at decade transitions. Clinicians should consider the potential influence of age perception in surgical decision-making.

title: Retinoblastoma management: achieving high standards of care
abstract: The current management of retinoblastoma involves chemotherapy by the intravenous, intra-arterial, intravitreous or intra-aqueous delivery routes. These routes can adequately control solid tumour, subretinal seeds, vitreous seeds or aqueous seeds. Intravenous chemotherapy using vincristine, etoposide and carboplatin is commonly used for retinoblastoma control. According to the International Classification of Retinoblastoma, intravenous chemotherapy provides globe salvage with tumour control in 96% of Group A, 90% of Group B and Group C, 68% of Group D and 32% of Group E eyes. Intra-arterial chemotherapy, using melphalan, topotecan and/or carboplatin with delivery from the femoral artery up to the ophthalmic artery to the eye, is particularly used for unilateral retinoblastoma. This alternative has more localised ocular complications but offers more powerful tumour control. Intravitreal chemotherapy, using melphalan and topotecan, can control vitreous seeding, but most specialists employ high-dose topotecan for control of vitreous seeds and some solid tumours and even subretinal seeds. Intra-aqueous chemotherapy, using melphalan or topotecan and can be effective for aqueous seeding. There is still a role for plaque radiotherapy in non-chemotherapy-responsive tumours and enucleation for massive disease that doesn't fully respond to chemotherapy or demonstrates high-risk disease. The management of retinoblastoma has evolved to the current day with several routes of chemotherapy delivery.

title: Identification of a translatable rabbit model for corneal endothelial dysfunction
abstract: Purpose To explore the potential of an adult rabbit descemetorhexis model to recapitulate the damage to the endothelium and Descemet's membrane (DM) seen in humans. Methods Five corneas of 5 female New Zealand rabbits aged 24-26 months underwent 5-mm descemetorhexis; five unwounded corneas from 5 rabbits served as controls. Animals were followed up for 12-week and post-surgical clinical evaluation was performed using slit-lamp, macro images, and optical coherence tomography (OCT). Histological and immunohistochemical analyses were performed post-sacrifice. Results Corneal transparency analysed by slit-lamp demonstrated that 2 weeks after descemetorhexis, all adult rabbits displayed grade 3 corneal opacity that was reduced to grade 2-3 and remained at this level until the study endpoint. Corroborating these results, quantitative analysis of macro images showed a significant reduction in corneal transparency during the entire follow-up period, with remarkable effect at 2 weeks (P + /K + -ATPase and Zonula occludens-1. An altered collagen matrix with myofibroblasts in the posterior stroma was also found in the surgical center compared with the other analyzed regions in both groups. Conclusions Our results indicate that descemetorhexis in adult rabbits could be a translatable corneal endothelial dysfunction (CED) model for studying the safety and efficacy of treatments for CED.

title: Persistent foetal vasculature: Developmental mechanisms, contemporary management and evolving therapeutics
abstract: Abstract Persistent foetal vasculature (PFV) is a spectrum of congenital malformations arising from incomplete regression of the hyaloid–tunica vasculosa lentis complex. Since Reese’s original description of persistent hyperplastic primary vitreous and Goldberg’s seminal reinterpretation of PFV as a unified developmental spectrum, our understanding has expanded through advances in genetics, imaging, and vitreoretinal surgery. PFV remains one of the most challenging causes of unilateral childhood visual loss. Although modern microsurgical techniques now deliver consistent anatomical success and globe preservation, functional vision is often limited by primary retinal and optic-nerve maldevelopment. This review traces the evolution of PFV management from its embryological basis to current surgical paradigms, integrating evidence from major series and highlighting practical lessons from contemporary vitreoretinal practice.

Deep learning–based prediction of one-year functional and structural outcomes in treatment-naïve DMO after anti-VEGF therapy
abstract: Abstract Purpose To evaluate whether baseline structural optical coherence tomography (OCT) scans contain prognostic information that can be used by deep learning models to predict one-year functional and anatomical outcomes in treatment-naïve diabetic macular oedema (DMO). Design Retrospective cohort study. Participants Eighty-seven eyes (74 patients) with treatment-naïve DMO receiving intravitreal anti-VEGF therapy. Methods Baseline OCT volumes were analysed using a deep learning regression model. The images were homogenised – preprocessed and transformed into a common reference frame – to streamline the learning task. The model predicted 12-month changes in best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) and central subfield thickness (CST). Main outcome measures Performance was assessed using 5-fold cross-validation and compared between original and preprocessed datasets. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis evaluated classification of responders versus non-responders, while occlusion sensitivity analysis identified image regions contributing most to predictions. Results Mean BCVA improved from 0.40 ± 0.40 to 0.33 ± 0.30 logMAR, and CST decreased from 390.2 ± 77.1 µm to 342.2 ± 76.3 µm (both p < 0.001). Prediction of BCVA change achieved an R² of 0.575, improving to 0.661 after preprocessing. CST prediction improved from R² = 0.447–0.633. Classification performance increased from AUC 0.65 to 0.71 for BCVA response and from 0.93 to 0.97 for CST response. Key predictive regions included the outer retina and retinal pigment epithelium. Conclusions Deep learning analysis of baseline OCT can predict one-year outcomes in DMO. Image homogenisation enhances performance, and responder identification suggests the potential utility of this approach for prognostic assessment and risk stratification, warranting further validation before clinical implementation.

title: Post-treatment residual masses in orbital lymphoma: incidence, risk factors, and prognostic impact
abstract: Purpose We aimed to evaluate the incidence and risk factors for residual masses (RMs) following first-line treatment of primary orbital lymphoma (OL) and identify predictors of local recurrence (LR) and systemic relapse (SR) among patients with RMs. Methods This retrospective study included 100 individuals with OL who received treatment and were followed for over 6 months. Clinical characteristics were reviewed, and treatment responses were assessed at 12 and 24 weeks post-treatment and at the last follow-up. Risk factors for RM presence, persistence, LR, and SR were analysed. Results The mean age was 57.1 years, with a male predominance (61%) and a median follow-up of 58.2 months. Histological subtypes included extranodal marginal zone lymphoma (EMZL, n = 85), diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL, n = 12), and mantle cell lymphoma (MCL, n = 3). Residual masses were identified in 73% of participants at 12 weeks post-treatment. Residual mass presence was significantly associated with tumour size ≥25 mm, AJCC N1/M1 stage, and location in the posterior orbit or with extraocular muscle involvement (each P Conclusion Post-treatment RMs were common in OL, particularly among individuals with advanced-stage, large, or posteriorly located tumours. Among those with RMs, AJCC N1 stage and high-grade histology were independent predictors of relapse. Given the risk of relapse despite standard first-line therapy, intensified treatment and closer surveillance should be considered in this high-risk subgroup.

abstract: Fig. 1: Efficacy, safety, and patient preference results from the Phase 3 PAGODA trial of the port delivery platform (PDS) with ranibizumab. Full size image PDS with ranibizumab Q24W showed comparable efficacy to Q4W intravitreal injections of ranibizumab, supporting continuous delivery of VEGF inhibition with a 6-month refill interval in the treatment of DMO, with no cases of endophthalmitis reported through Week 64. A majority of patients preferred PDS over intravitreal injections.

title: Combined limbal dysmaturation and microcyst like epithelial changes with corneal nerve alterations of a novel anti nectin-4-MMAE antibody drug conjugate
Prelaminar hyperreflective lines in non-arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy
abstract: Abstract Objective To compare clinical and imaging features of non-arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy (NAION) with and without optic disc drusen (ODD)-like features, including ODD and hyperreflective lines (HRLs), and assess the impact of HRLs on disease outcomes. Methods This is a retrospective analysis of 17 NAION patients with ODD (ODD-AION), 25 NAION patients with HRLs only (HRL-AION), and 45 NAION patients without ODD-like features from a dataset of 177 NAION patients. ODD-like features were diagnosed via the enhanced-depth imaging optical coherence tomography (EDI-OCT). Patients underwent full ophthalmic assessment, including visual acuity, Humphrey visual field mean deviation, ganglion cell complex (GCC), retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL), Bruch’s membrane opening (BMO), and flavoprotein fluorescence (FPF) imaging. Results ODD-like features were present in 23.7% of the NAION cohort and were associated with younger age at NAION onset and better visual acuity (adjusted p = 0.027), with higher GCC and RNFL thickness. BMO was significantly smaller in eyes with ODD-like features. ODD-AION showed earlier onset and female predominance, whereas HRL-AION resembled typical NAION demographically but had more favorable structural and visual outcomes. HRL-AION eyes demonstrated a lower global FPF signal when compared with NAION and ODD-AION. Conclusion Like ODD, the presence of HRLs in NAION is associated with crowding of the optic nerve head and better structural and functional outcomes, but not with a young onset of the disease. This study highlights the heterogeneity of NAION and the role of EDI-OCT findings in understanding determinants of outcomes.

title: Large language models as internal consistency checkers for ophthalmic manuscripts
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in scientific writing, while their potential application to editorial assessment and peer review has attracted growing interest [ 1 , 2 , 3 ]. However, their ability to identify internal inconsistencies within scientific manuscripts remains poorly characterised. We evaluated four contemporary LLMs as automated consistency checkers using published ophthalmic literature.

abstract: Reliable procedure identification in electronic medical records (EMRs) is important for clinical registries, trial recruitment, quality assurance, and operative log validation. Administrative coding may not accurately reflect clinical diagnoses or procedures. In an Australian two-hospital study, only 53.9% of ophthalmology procedures were correctly coded [ 1 ].

Personalised ILM peeling for Myopic traction maculopathy
abstract: Purpose To introduce a novel ILM peeling technique for S2 and S3 retinoschisis, termed 'Personalised ILM peeling', which selectively peels the ILM only within the schisis area while minimising postoperative complications. Methods 10 eyes from 9 patients with MRS underwent 'Personalised ILM peeling'. Preoperatively, the OCT radial scans, 3D Wide scans and retinal thickness map were comprehensively evaluated to delineate the extent of the schisis area and determine the specific region requiring ILM peel. Pre- and postoperative visual acuity, retinal thickness, including retinoschisis height, and visual field were analyzed. Results No case of recurrence were observed during a follow-up period exceeding 24 months. No Postoperative complications occurred in any of the 10 cases. Compared with preoperative measurements, postoperative visual acuity and retinal thickness, including retinoschisis height, demonstrated significant improvement. Conclusions Personalised ILM peeling is proposed as a novel, minimally invasive surgical approach for MRS. Many cases with high myopia are accompanied by visual field defects and it is expected that this will avoid damage to the fragile retina and nerve fibres.

Hydrus microstent combined with cataract surgery or used alone: cost-utility analysis for UK
abstract: Abstract Background Minimally invasive glaucoma surgery (MIGS) has the potential to become standard of care for patients with primary open angle glaucoma (POAG), whether combined with cataract surgery (CS) or as a standalone procedure. This study provides evidence of cost-effectiveness for Hydrus Microstent for both indications in UK healthcare settings. Methods A cohort Markov model simulated the natural history of POAG to assess costs and quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) over a 15-year horizon, comparing Hydrus Microstent + CS with CS alone, and Hydrus Microstent to iStent standalone. Patient progression across glaucoma severity health states was modelled using a rate of progression (RoP) derived from 5-year visual field loss data in HORIZON trial (for mild to moderate POAG) and by trial-based annual number of medications from COMPARE trial (for moderate POAG), respectively. Conducted from the public healthcare payer perspective, model inputs were derived from UK publicly available sources and/or publications. Both deterministic and probabilistic analyses (PA) were performed. Results When compared with CS alone, Hydrus + CS was estimated to generate 0.334 more QALYs but £604 higher costs over the 15-year time horizon. When comparing Hydrus to iStent, Hydrus had £534 in projected savings and generated 0.068 more QALYs. The PA showed that the probability of Hydrus + CS being cost-effective compared to CS alone is 87.6%, and about 71.5% when compared to iStent. The results were consistent across scenario analyses. Conclusions Hydrus implantation is a cost-effective strategy both in combination with CS (for mild-to-moderate POAG) and as a standalone procedure (for moderate POAG) in UK healthcare settings.

Making better use of patients’ time: feasibility of performing self-administered vision assessments in waiting rooms
abstract: Abstract Background Patients often spend significant time in clinic waiting rooms. This study assessed the feasibility of using this “wasted” time to perform self-administered vision assessments directly within the waiting area. Methods Glaucoma patients attending routine appointments were asked to complete either a pen-and-paper (SpotChecks) or digital (PopCSF) contrast sensitivity (CS) test. Ambient illuminance, background noise, and crowd levels were recorded to assess potential environmental confounds. Test durations and patient feedback were recorded. Visual-Functioning Index-7 (VF-7) and Pelli-Robson CS (reference) test results were collected for comparison. Results Of 173 patients approached, 155 (89.6%) agreed to participate, and 151(97.4%) participants completed testing before their appointment (77/78 pen-and-paper; 74/74 digital). Environmental factors had no significant impact (all P > 0.05). Median completion times were 3.0 {2.6–4.5} minutes (pen-and-paper) and 2.5 {2.0–3.5} minutes (digital). Age did not impact the pen-and-paper test duration ( P = 0.944) but weakly correlated with the digital test duration ( r digital = 0.27, P = 0.020). Functional CS scores correlated with Pelli-Robson reference measurements ( r pen-and-paper = 0.81; r digital = 0.62 ) , age ( r pen-and-paper = –0.58 ; r digital = – 0.37), logMAR visual acuity ( r pen-and-paper = – 0.42 ; r digital = –0.44), and visual field mean deviation scores ( r pen-and-paper = –0.54 ; r digital = –0.63). Both tests were highly acceptable to patients ( > 80% on all questions). Visit durations were longer for participants (109 vs 88 min, P = 0.007), but this was attributed to consenting and related research activities rather than the tests themselves. Conclusions This proof-of-concept study demonstrates that it is feasible for patients to self-administer portable vision tests in clinic waiting rooms. Using CS as a representative example, this approach may enable additional data collection, potentially improving patient management, clinic flow, and/or patient satisfaction.

title: The Royal College of Ophthalmologists’ National Ophthalmology Database: report 15, severe vision loss following cataract surgery
abstract: Abstract Background/objectives To investigate rates of severe vision loss post-cataract surgery. Subjects/methods Post-cataract severe vision loss (SVL) was defined as a loss of ≥0.60 LogMAR between preoperative presenting visual acuity and postoperative visual acuity. The term ‘legally blind’ was used for eyes with a corrected visual acuity worse than 1.30 LogMAR. Between 2010 and 2024, there were 1,750,553 eligible operations performed on 1,217,267 patients by 3766 surgeons from 132 centres supplying data to the Royal College of Ophthalmologists National Ophthalmology Database Cataract Audit. Results Severe vision loss was recorded in 3723 (0.21%) eyes, including 3 eyes (2 patients) from 2 718 immediate sequential bilateral cataract surgery (ISBCS) eyes. The highest observed SVL rate was 10.68% for eyes recorded as left aphakic after surgery and the second highest observed SVL rate (3.32%) was when posterior capsular rupture occurred. The SVL rate was higher than the overall rate for eyes with previous intravitreal injections (0.76%), eyes with optic nerve or central nervous system problems (0.74%), age-related macular degeneration (0.52%), previous vitrectomy surgery (0.49%), diabetic retinopathy (0.45%), glaucoma (0.42%) or corneal pathology (0.33%). Of 1,642,386 (93.8%) eyes that were not preoperatively legally blind, 2731 (0.2%) were postoperatively legally blind. Of these, 2294 (84.0%) eyes experienced severe vision loss. Conclusions Severe vision loss from any cause following cataract surgery occurs infrequently. However, it has a higher prevalence in eyes left aphakic, when PCR occurs and for certain ocular comorbidities.

title: Alternate eye patching improves long-term alignment stability after surgery for intermittent exotropia: a randomised controlled trial
abstract: Abstract Background/objectives Postoperative exodrift remains a major challenge following surgical correction of intermittent exotropia (IXT), and evidence supporting adjunctive strategies to improve long-term alignment is limited. This study evaluated the effect of alternate eye patching on 12-month postoperative alignment stability after successful surgical correction in divergence excess IXT. Subjects/methods This randomised clinical trial was conducted at an institutional tertiary care centre and included 60 children (3–12 years) undergoing bilateral lateral rectus recession who were randomised only after confirmation of early postoperative alignment ( ≤ 10 prism dioptres [PD]), creating a post-success randomised design to evaluate the effect of alternate eye patching on alignment maintenance. Participants were assigned to alternate eye patching (Group A) or standard postoperative care (Group B). Patching was prescribed for 1 h daily per eye for 3 months. Patients were followed for 12 months. The primary outcome was alignment stability ( ≤ 10 PD). Secondary outcomes included exodrift ( > 10 PD), mean deviation, and reoperation rate. Results At 12 months, alignment stability was significantly higher in Group A compared with Group B (83.3% vs 60.0%, p = 0.045). Significant exodrift occurred less frequently in Group A (16.7% vs 40.0%, p = 0.045). Mean postoperative deviation was lower in Group A at all follow-up visits ( p < 0.05). No patients in Group A required reoperation compared with 10% in Group B, although this difference was not statistically significant ( p = 0.112). Conclusion Alternate eye patching may improve postoperative alignment stability and reduce postoperative exodrift for divergence excess intermittent exotropia. Early postoperative modulation of binocular visual balance may contribute to improved long-term alignment outcomes. Clinical trial registry Pan African Clinical Trial Registry ( PACTR202505751499770 ), registered on May 14, 2025. https://pactr.samrc.ac.za/
